newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan stocks hit second record high.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan stocks hit second record high.

text.p: Caracas stocks rose to record highs for the second consecutive session as investors bought into growing confidence in Venezuela's economic prospects, traders said.
The market's 19-share .IBC index gained 0.52 percent to close at 4,804.12 points according to preliminary figures from the stock exchange.
Among traded issues, 18 rose, nine fell and 14 closed flat.
"Venezuela is full of good news at the moment and Brady debt continues to rise, which is a good sign of returning confidence," said Profimerca borker Miguel Gonzalez.
Bullish sentiment infected stocks as Venezuelan Brady bonds hit record intra-day highs, with investors -- "mostly foreign" said Gonzalez -- focusing on blue-chips.
Heavy buying was reported for market-leader Electricidad de Caracas, up 7.95 bolivars to close at 419.94, and foods producer Mavesa, up 1.50 to close at 126.50.
Overall, however, trading volume remained slight, traders said. Just under nine million shares traded to a total value of 1.32 billion bolivars ($2.8 million).
